text: RP2 Colloquium 2 | frequency group x syllable length
textPreview: RP2 Colloquium 2 | frequency group x syllable length

text:
Dang Nhat Quang
Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Tibor Kiss
12 June 2026
textPreview: Dang Nhat Quang | Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Tibor Kiss | 12 June 2026

text: I will start by giving the basic shape of the project. This is a Vietnamese lexical decision task, and the two main predictors I am focusing on are frequency group and syllable length. The headline numbers are here so the audience immediately sees that this is an actual collected dataset, not only a design proposal.
The talk follows the project from linguistic motivation to cautious preliminary results.
textPreview: The talk follows the project from linguistic motivation to cautious preliminary results.

text: syllables are spaced, lexical words may be multi-syllabic
textPreview: syllables are spaced, lexical words may be multi-syllabic

text: participant, item, trial, RT, response checks
textPreview: participant, item, trial, RT, response checks

text: Aim for the presentation: show that the experiment is methodologically defensible, reproducible, and interpreted carefully.
textPreview: Aim for the presentation: show that the experiment is methodologically defensible, reproducible, and interpreted carefully.

text: Here I want to give the audience the route through the talk. I begin with the linguistic motivation, then move into the experimental design and cleaning, and only after that I discuss the preliminary results. The main message is that the project is already analyzable, but the interpretation is still cautious.
Quốc ngữ is the current endpoint of a layered writing history, not a single-inventor story.
textPreview: Quốc ngữ is the current endpoint of a layered writing history, not a single-inventor story.

text: Sources: Fernandes & Assunção, 2017; DeFrancis, 1977; Encyclopaedia Britannica, 2026
textPreview: Sources: Fernandes & Assunção, 2017; DeFrancis, 1977; Encyclopaedia Britannica, 2026

text:
Latin-based Vietnamese
missionary codification, later mass adoption
textPreview: Latin-based Vietnamese | missionary codification, later mass adoption

text: The modern script was shaped by several European missionaries. Portuguese Jesuits were central in early romanization; Alexandre de Rhodes published an influential Vietnamese-Portuguese-Latin dictionary in 1651. Later French colonial schooling/administration and Vietnamese print culture helped Quốc ngữ spread.
textPreview: The modern script was shaped by several European missionaries. Portuguese Jesuits were central in early romanization; Alexandre de Rhodes...

text: Why this matters here: the modern script is alphabetic and spaced, but spacing does not make Vietnamese word boundaries simple.
textPreview: Why this matters here: the modern script is alphabetic and spaced, but spacing does not make Vietnamese word boundaries simple.

text: This slide is mainly background, so I would not spend too long on it. The important correction is that Quốc ngữ was not created by one single French or Italian person. It developed through several historical stages, with early missionary romanization and later institutional spread.
Vietnamese spaces often separate syllables, while lexical words may contain several syllables.
textPreview: Vietnamese spaces often separate syllables, while lexical words may contain several syllables.

text: Sources: Ha, 2003; Đinh et al., 2008; Verdonschot et al., 2022
textPreview: Sources: Ha, 2003; Đinh et al., 2008; Verdonschot et al., 2022

text:
space ≠ lexical word boundary

This is why Vietnamese word segmentation is non-trivial for NLP and for stimulus selection.
textPreview: space ≠ lexical word boundary |  | This is why Vietnamese word segmentation is non-trivial for NLP and for stimulus selection.

text: This is the key linguistic reason for the project. In Vietnamese, spaces often separate syllables, but lexical words can have more than one syllable. So I use this example to show why syllable length is meaningful, and also why I cannot simply treat every space-separated unit as a word.
Corpus text was converted into review data and then into final LDT stimuli.
textPreview: Corpus text was converted into review data and then into final LDT stimuli.

text: N-grams are candidates, not final lexical words.
textPreview: N-grams are candidates, not final lexical words.

freq = pd.concat(pd.read_csv(f) for f in files)

items = (freq

    syllable_length=lambda d: d.lexical_item.str.split().str.len(),
    log_frequency=lambda d: np.log(d.frequency))
  .query("1 <= syllable_length <= 4")
  .drop_duplicates("lexical_item"))

review_sheet = items.sort_values(["syllable_length", "log_frequency"])

text: Traceable dataset: corpus frequency -> filtered candidates -> review/survey -> final stimuli.
textPreview: Traceable dataset: corpus frequency -> filtered candidates -> review/survey -> final stimuli.

text: This slide explains where the stimulus data came from. I start from corpus-derived frequency tables, use those to build candidate items, and then move into review and final stimulus selection. I would emphasize that the code is a simplified version of the pipeline: the important point is traceability, not that tokenization alone solved the lexical problem.
Do frequency group and syllable length predict Vietnamese lexical-decision response times?
textPreview: Do frequency group and syllable length predict Vietnamese lexical-decision response times?

text: How do corpus frequency group and syllable length affect log reaction time for correct Vietnamese real-word responses?
textPreview: How do corpus frequency group and syllable length affect log reaction time for correct Vietnamese real-word responses?

text: High-frequency words should be recognized faster than low-frequency words.
textPreview: High-frequency words should be recognized faster than low-frequency words.

text: Longer syllable length should increase RT because longer words require more visual/lexical processing.
textPreview: Longer syllable length should increase RT because longer words require more visual/lexical processing.

text: The size of the frequency effect may vary across syllable lengths.
textPreview: The size of the frequency effect may vary across syllable lengths.

text: Interpretation rule: interaction evidence will be treated as preliminary unless it is stable across diagnostics and follow-up checks.
textPreview: Interpretation rule: interaction evidence will be treated as preliminary unless it is stable across diagnostics and follow-up checks.

text: Here I state the research question directly. The dependent variable is log reaction time for correct real-word responses. The hypotheses are standard but still useful: higher frequency should make responses faster, longer syllable length should slow responses, and the interaction is something I test carefully rather than overstate.
The real-word design is balanced: 3 frequency groups x 4 syllable lengths, within participant.
textPreview: The real-word design is balanced: 3 frequency groups x 4 syllable lengths, within participant.

text: cell value = number of real-word items
textPreview: cell value = number of real-word items

text: All participants see all main trials in randomized order.
textPreview: All participants see all main trials in randomized order.

text: This slide is about experimental balance. Each participant saw the same full set of trials, and the real-word part is balanced across three frequency groups and four syllable lengths. I would point out that this balance is what makes the later model easier to interpret.
Pseudowords keep the task genuinely lexical: participants must distinguish words from nonwords.
textPreview: Pseudowords keep the task genuinely lexical: participants must distinguish words from nonwords.

text:
núi
loại sản phẩm
điện thoại di động

bệc viện ← bệnh viện
mối quan hế ← mối quan hệ
trính độ học vấn ← trình độ học vấn

text: Pseudoword construction changes a syllable while keeping the item Vietnamese-like enough for the task.
textPreview: Pseudoword construction changes a syllable while keeping the item Vietnamese-like enough for the task.

text: Here I explain why pseudowords are necessary. If participants only saw real words, the task could become a simple reading task. The pseudowords force a real lexical decision, and they also give me an accuracy check for whether participants are taking the task seriously.
The procedure is short, randomized, and keyboard-based to keep lexical decisions clean.
textPreview: The procedure is short, randomized, and keyboard-based to keep lexical decisions clean.

text: Main-trial order is randomized for each participant.
textPreview: Main-trial order is randomized for each participant.

text:
F key: word
J key: nonword
textPreview: F key: word | J key: nonword

text: This is the practical task flow. Participants do a few practice trials first, then the main randomized block. I would be careful with the F and J point: the keys help make responses fast and balanced, but they do not magically remove all bias.
The design reduces common task artifacts and monitors the ones it cannot remove.
textPreview: The design reduces common task artifacts and monitors the ones it cannot remove.

text: Practice trials before the main task; randomized main trials.
textPreview: Practice trials before the main task; randomized main trials.

text: Pseudowords require word/nonword discrimination; QC checks one-key overuse.
textPreview: Pseudowords require word/nonword discrimination; QC checks one-key overuse.

text: F/J supports balanced keyboard responding, but does not fully eliminate side bias.
textPreview: F/J supports balanced keyboard responding, but does not fully eliminate side bias.

text: Monitor accuracy, missing RTs, unusually fast RTs, and one-key patterns.
textPreview: Monitor accuracy, missing RTs, unusually fast RTs, and one-key patterns.

text: Important wording: F/J helps reduce motor-response delay and makes responses more balanced; it does not completely remove bias.
textPreview: Important wording: F/J helps reduce motor-response delay and makes responses more balanced; it does not completely remove bias.

text: This slide is my bias-control slide. I want to show that I know the task can have practice effects, response bias, side bias, and fatigue. The design reduces some of these risks, and the QC checks help me detect them, but I should not claim that the design removes them completely.
A short PsychoPy video can show the task more clearly than more procedure text.
textPreview: A short PsychoPy video can show the task more clearly than more procedure text.

text: Show: stimulus display → F/J keypress → next randomized trial
textPreview: Show: stimulus display → F/J keypress → next randomized trial

text: This is a placeholder for the demo video. In the actual talk, I can pause here and show a very short clip of the PsychoPy task. The goal is just to make the procedure concrete before I move into data handling.
The project is reproducible from experiment implementation through R Markdown modeling.
textPreview: The project is reproducible from experiment implementation through R Markdown modeling.

text: This is the full workflow slide. I want the audience to see that the analysis did not jump straight from experiment to model. The data moved through PsychoPy and Pavlovia, then CSV export, Python cleaning and QC, and finally R Markdown and mixed-effects modeling.
Cleaning was designed to preserve raw data while making analysis copies auditable.
textPreview: Cleaning was designed to preserve raw data while making analysis copies auditable.

textPreview: trial_id and stimulus list matched against final design

textPreview: raw CSVs are read, not modified

text: This is where I defend the cleaning process. I would say that raw data were preserved, and the cleaning script created analysis copies. The checks here are basic but important: encoding, participant IDs, trial counts, response mapping, RT conversion, log RT, missing values, and stimulus validation.
The current dataset passes the main participant, trial, and stimulus-validation checks.
textPreview: The current dataset passes the main participant, trial, and stimulus-validation checks.

Stimulus file readable
120 unique main trial IDs
72 real words, 48 pseudowords
Every trial_id has 48 presentations
No unexpected trial IDs
Raw data were not modified

text: Current stage: ready for Colloquium 2 presentation, but results remain preliminary.
textPreview: Current stage: ready for Colloquium 2 presentation, but results remain preliminary.

text: This slide gives the current data status. The main point is that the dataset passes the major checks: 48 participants, the expected number of trials, and no flagged participants. I also want to be honest that the RT model uses only correct real-word responses, while accuracy is handled separately.
The workflow keeps raw data, cleaned analysis copies, QC outputs, and the analysis report separate.
textPreview: The workflow keeps raw data, cleaned analysis copies, QC outputs, and the analysis report separate.

text: Reproducibility principle: every transformation has a named script or output file.
textPreview: Reproducibility principle: every transformation has a named script or output file.

text: Here I frame the project as reproducible. Every transformation has a named input and output, so the analysis can be rerun. This matters because the presentation is not just showing results; it is showing that the results come from a controlled pipeline.
Log RT and mixed-effects models match the structure of repeated lexical-decision data.
textPreview: Log RT and mixed-effects models match the structure of repeated lexical-decision data.

text: Sources: Baayen et al., 2008; Bates et al., 2015; Ratcliff, 1993; Whelan, 2008
textPreview: Sources: Baayen et al., 2008; Bates et al., 2015; Ratcliff, 1993; Whelan, 2008

text:
Reaction-time data are typically right-skewed.

Using log_rt reduces skew and makes linear-model assumptions more plausible.

Diagnostics are still checked.

Each participant sees many items.

Each item is seen by many participants.

Random intercepts account for participant and item variability.

Correct real-word main trials only

n = 3,306
participants = 48
items = 72
textPreview: Correct real-word main trials only |  | n = 3,306 | participants = 48 | items = 72

text: Accuracy is summarized separately because pseudowords are central for task quality but not part of the real-word RT model.
textPreview: Accuracy is summarized separately because pseudowords are central for task quality but not part of the real-word RT model.

text: This slide explains the statistical choices in plain language. Reaction times are skewed, so log RT is more appropriate than raw RT. A mixed-effects model is also necessary because responses are repeated within participants and items.
The main model estimates frequency, syllable length, and their interaction with participant and item intercepts.
textPreview: The main model estimates frequency, syllable length, and their interaction with participant and item intercepts.

text:
Observations: 3,306
Participants: 48
Items: 72
Singular fit: false
textPreview: Observations: 3,306 | Participants: 48 | Items: 72 | Singular fit: false

text: This structure avoids treating 3,306 rows as fully independent observations.
textPreview: This structure avoids treating 3,306 rows as fully independent observations.

text: This is the model slide. I would explain the formula slowly: frequency group, syllable length, and their interaction are fixed effects, while participant and trial ID are random intercepts. The model is meant to respect the structure of the experiment rather than treating every row as fully independent.
Descriptively, high-frequency words are faster and longer words are slower.
textPreview: Descriptively, high-frequency words are faster and longer words are slower.

text: Here I start the results section descriptively. The boxplots show the two big patterns: high-frequency words are faster, and longer words are slower. I would avoid making strong claims here and say that this is the descriptive pattern before model-based interpretation.
The frequency advantage may vary by syllable length, but the interaction is modest.
textPreview: The frequency advantage may vary by syllable length, but the interaction is modest.

text:
Interaction model improves fit over the additive model.

Likelihood-ratio p = .0449.

Treat as evidence of possible variation, not a large final conclusion.
textPreview: Interaction model improves fit over the additive model. |  | Likelihood-ratio p = .0449. |  | Treat as evidence of possible variation, no...

text: Result wording: frequency and length effects are clearer than the interaction.
textPreview: Result wording: frequency and length effects are clearer than the interaction.

text: This slide focuses on the interaction pattern. The lines are not perfectly parallel, so there may be some interaction between frequency and length. But I would present it as modest and preliminary, not as the main conclusion.
Adding frequency and syllable length improves model fit; the interaction adds only a small increment.
textPreview: Adding frequency and syllable length improves model fit; the interaction adds only a small increment.

text: Adding syllable length gives the biggest model-fit improvement.
textPreview: Adding syllable length gives the biggest model-fit improvement.

text: The interaction improves fit, but weakly. It should guide follow-up checks rather than stand alone.
textPreview: The interaction improves fit, but weakly. It should guide follow-up checks rather than stand alone.

text: This model comparison slide is important because it shows what each predictor adds. Frequency improves fit, syllable length gives the largest improvement, and the interaction adds a smaller improvement. I would use this slide to explain why my main interpretation focuses most on frequency and length.
Model checks support cautious reporting, not overconfident final claims.
textPreview: Model checks support cautious reporting, not overconfident final claims.

text: Adjusted GVIF values remain below common concern thresholds.
textPreview: Adjusted GVIF values remain below common concern thresholds.

text: RT diagnostics should be reviewed again before thesis-level claims.
textPreview: RT diagnostics should be reviewed again before thesis-level claims.

text: Here I discuss diagnostics. I do not want to pretend the model is perfect, because RT data usually have tails and some deviation. The point is that the diagnostics look acceptable for a preliminary presentation, but they still support cautious reporting.
Accuracy and response QC suggest participants generally performed the task seriously.
textPreview: Accuracy and response QC suggest participants generally performed the task seriously.

text: Pseudoword accuracy is lower than word accuracy, but still high enough to show nonword discrimination.
textPreview: Pseudoword accuracy is lower than word accuracy, but still high enough to show nonword discrimination.

text: This slide gives the task-quality evidence. Word accuracy is high, and pseudoword accuracy is lower but still reasonable. I would say this supports the idea that participants were generally doing the lexical decision task, not just pressing randomly.
The strongest preliminary story is frequency plus syllable length, with a tentative interaction.
textPreview: The strongest preliminary story is frequency plus syllable length, with a tentative interaction.

text: High-frequency words were responded to faster than low-frequency words.
textPreview: High-frequency words were responded to faster than low-frequency words.

text: Mean RT increased from one-syllable to four-syllable words.
textPreview: Mean RT increased from one-syllable to four-syllable words.

text: Possible variation in the frequency effect, but modest.
textPreview: Possible variation in the frequency effect, but modest.

text: Cautious interpretation: lexical-decision RT reflects lexical processing plus task-decision processes, so the results should not be reduced to pure lexical access.
textPreview: Cautious interpretation: lexical-decision RT reflects lexical processing plus task-decision processes, so the results should not be reduc...

text: This is the main interpretation slide. My strongest claim is that frequency and syllable length both matter in the expected directions. The interaction is interesting, but I would keep it secondary until more robustness checks are done.
The current analysis is ready for discussion, but not yet a final thesis conclusion.
textPreview: The current analysis is ready for discussion, but not yet a final thesis conclusion.

text: N = 48 reaches the minimum target but is still a minimum sample.
textPreview: N = 48 reaches the minimum target but is still a minimum sample.

text: Pseudowords should be reviewed for plausibility and matching before final reporting.
textPreview: Pseudowords should be reviewed for plausibility and matching before final reporting.

text: Frequency source and item matching may need dispersion/register checks.
textPreview: Frequency source and item matching may need dispersion/register checks.

text: The current model uses random intercepts; richer structures can be tested if stable.
textPreview: The current model uses random intercepts; richer structures can be tested if stable.

text: The project does not solve full Vietnamese word segmentation.
textPreview: The project does not solve full Vietnamese word segmentation.

text: Review diagnostics, check sensitivity decisions, consider supplementary accuracy models, and refine the interaction interpretation.
textPreview: Review diagnostics, check sensitivity decisions, consider supplementary accuracy models, and refine the interaction interpretation.

text: This slide is deliberately cautious. The analysis is ready to discuss, but it is not the final thesis conclusion yet. I would mention the sample size, pseudoword plausibility, item matching, and possible richer random-effects structures as things to strengthen next.
The six-month plan moves from design and data collection toward final modeling and write-up.
textPreview: The six-month plan moves from design and data collection toward final modeling and write-up.

text: Data collection, cleaning, first R Markdown analysis, figures, tables, and diagnostics are ready. Final interpretation and write-up still need review.
textPreview: Data collection, cleaning, first R Markdown analysis, figures, tables, and diagnostics are ready. Final interpretation and write-up still...

text: Here I show that the project has a realistic path forward. The next phase is not to redesign everything; it is to rerun, check robustness, review items, and write the results carefully. This gives the committee confidence that the project is manageable.
